text:
The Blackhawks played in Calgary the week Connor Bedard is set to have surgery on his right shoulder, and their best players without him were a 38-year-old winger and a young defenseman. Sam Rinzel won it 4:45 into overtime, Patrick Kane had a goal and two assists, and Chicago beat the Flames 4-3. The headlines going in had Chicago still chasing its first road win.

Calgary had the early edge. Ryan Strome scored midway through the first, and the Flames led in expected goals (the quality of the chances each team got) 1.39 to 0.72 after one period. Then Chicago scored three times in just over three minutes early in the second: Roman Kantserov from Kane, Ryan Donato on a batted puck, and Kane himself on a power-play slap shot. The Flames clawed back. Jonathan Castagna, who scored his first two NHL goals earlier this month, cut it to 3-2, and Yegor Sharangovich tied it on the power play 1:14 into the third.

Over 60 minutes Calgary was the better team. The Flames out-attempted Chicago 73 to 51 and had 3.63 expected goals to 3.36, and Spencer Knight was the reason it went to overtime, saving 33 of 36 shots, including Joel Farabee's 32% chance in the second. Overtime was all Chicago, 1.32 expected goals to none. Dustin Wolf made a big stop in overtime, and moments later Rinzel, set up by Kane and Kantserov, ended it. Our replays had it close: 54% Calgary.

Rinzel played 26:12 and took six shots. The Athletic's Mark Lazerus noted he has twelve points in his last five games, which is the kind of run that can change how a team sees a young defenseman. Kane, who turned 38 this week, put seven shots on goal. Scott Powers pointed out that the Moore-Nazar-Kane line has been among the league's better ones by shot share this season.

For Calgary, Strome was the first star with a goal and an assist, and Zayne Parekh, whose breakout has been one of the Flames' good stories, picked up an assist in 21:42. The Flames are also playing without Kevin Bahl for the season. Losing at home when the chances favored you is the frustrating kind of night, and the standings won't care about the expected goals.
headline: Rinzel wins it in overtime for Bedard-less Blackhawks
